    The dimension induction (Proposition 8.3) in characteristic two #

    The source paper. The induction is run on representation-finite ray tables T (Definition 3.9: kT is its own ray linearization). Its conclusion is the weight lifting property of T (Proposition 8.3(3), in the form hW used by Theorem 9.1):

    • a disconnected table splits into two unions of components with fewer rays;
    • for a connected table, B = kT is basic and representation-finite; the characteristic-two step (exists_normedRayBasis_char2) presents B by the ray table P of its algebra A₀ (Proposition 8.3(2)), and T presents B as well (self_rayPres); so the two tables are isomorphic (Lemma 3.6), P is connected, and its weights lift by Proposition 7.2.

    Corollary 10.5 enters the characteristic-two step and itself uses the induction hypothesis (through Lemma 9.2 and Theorem 9.1); here it is the hypothesis Cor105Hyp.
